title: Zuriel Original-Language Word Study Collection — Batch 2
description: Twenty additional context-sensitive Hebrew and Greek word-study cards. These are lexical study aids, not verse-specific parsing or exhaustive lexicon definitions.
editorialPolicy: Original-language glosses are concise aids; inspect syntax and context in each passage.
No Strong's identifiers, morphology or pronunciation are asserted without source verification.
Do not derive theology from etymology alone; context governs meaning.
Where a term has a broad semantic range, the entry names that range rather than imposing one English equivalent.

entries.contextualGloss: Eternal or belonging to the age; in New Testament contexts it can describe life, judgement and realities associated with God's enduring purpose.
entries.interpretiveCaution: Do not reduce the word to a bare duration formula; examine the noun it modifies and the argument of the passage.
entries.morphologyStatus: Lexeme-level study only; no verse-specific inflection or parsing is asserted.

entries.contextualGloss: Resurrection or a rising; the New Testament uses it for the raising of the dead and, centrally, Jesus' resurrection.
entries.interpretiveCaution: Distinguish the resurrection event from metaphorical uses of rising language and read the surrounding argument.
entries.morphologyStatus: Lexeme-level study only; no verse-specific inflection or parsing is asserted.

entries.contextualGloss: Release, remission or forgiveness; the word can carry the image of release from debt or captivity.
entries.interpretiveCaution: Its sense is shaped by context; do not assume every occurrence describes precisely the same aspect of forgiveness.
entries.morphologyStatus: Lexeme-level study only; no verse-specific inflection or parsing is asserted.

entries.contextualGloss: Heart; the inner person, including thought, desire, intention and moral orientation, not merely emotion.
entries.interpretiveCaution: Ancient heart-language often includes thinking and willing; avoid importing a modern emotion-only meaning.
entries.morphologyStatus: Lexeme-level study only; no verse-specific inflection or parsing is asserted.

entries.contextualGloss: To call, summon or name; context may describe an invitation, vocation, summons or naming.
entries.interpretiveCaution: Do not treat every use as a technical term for one doctrine of calling; observe the subject, object and setting.
entries.morphologyStatus: Lexeme-level study only; no verse-specific inflection or parsing is asserted.

entries.contextualGloss: To judge, decide or evaluate; the word can describe judicial judgement, discernment or a decision.
entries.interpretiveCaution: The verb does not always mean condemn; read whether the passage concerns evaluation, verdict or condemnation.
entries.morphologyStatus: Lexeme-level study only; no verse-specific inflection or parsing is asserted.

entries.contextualGloss: To speak or utter; a common verb whose significance depends on speaker, audience and content.
entries.interpretiveCaution: Do not assign a special spiritual meaning to the verb in every occurrence; ordinary speech is also described with it.
entries.morphologyStatus: Lexeme-level study only; no verse-specific inflection or parsing is asserted.

entries.contextualGloss: Testimony or witness; a report or attestation that supports what is being claimed.
entries.interpretiveCaution: Distinguish the testimony itself from the person who bears witness and from later technical uses of martyrdom.
entries.morphologyStatus: Lexeme-level study only; no verse-specific inflection or parsing is asserted.

entries.contextualGloss: To remain, abide or continue; John's writings often use it for enduring relationship and continuity.
entries.interpretiveCaution: The metaphor of abiding must be read in its immediate context; do not reduce it to a single devotional technique.
entries.morphologyStatus: Lexeme-level study only; no verse-specific inflection or parsing is asserted.

entries.contextualGloss: To know or understand; in the New Testament it commonly expresses knowledge or awareness.
entries.interpretiveCaution: Do not infer a fixed hierarchy between this verb and other Greek verbs for knowing; usage overlaps and context governs.
entries.morphologyStatus: Lexeme-level study only; no verse-specific inflection or parsing is asserted.

entries.contextualGloss: To fill, make full or fulfil; the New Testament uses it for fullness, completion and fulfilment of Scripture.
entries.interpretiveCaution: The English word fulfil can hide different senses; examine whether the context concerns completion, filling or fulfilment.
entries.morphologyStatus: Lexeme-level study only; no verse-specific inflection or parsing is asserted.

entries.contextualGloss: Prayer; a common New Testament noun for prayer or the act/place of prayer.
entries.interpretiveCaution: The noun itself does not specify every feature of prayer; the passage supplies its content and posture.
entries.morphologyStatus: Lexeme-level study only; no verse-specific inflection or parsing is asserted.

entries.contextualGloss: Child or offspring; it can describe a physical child and, figuratively, a person in a relationship of belonging.
entries.interpretiveCaution: Distinguish literal family references from metaphorical uses, and read the relationship being described.
entries.morphologyStatus: Lexeme-level study only; no verse-specific inflection or parsing is asserted.

entries.contextualGloss: Will, desire or purpose; often used of God's will, but it can also describe human intention.
entries.interpretiveCaution: Identify whose will is in view and whether the passage concerns desire, purpose or an intended action.
entries.morphologyStatus: Lexeme-level study only; no verse-specific inflection or parsing is asserted.

entries.contextualGloss: To serve or care for; in many Gospel contexts it means to heal or treat the sick.
entries.interpretiveCaution: Do not assume every occurrence has the same nuance; the object and narrative context clarify whether healing or service is meant.
entries.morphologyStatus: Lexeme-level study only; no verse-specific inflection or parsing is asserted.

entries.contextualGloss: Affliction, distress or tribulation; imagery of pressure describes hardship experienced by people.
entries.interpretiveCaution: The word does not by itself identify the cause or duration of suffering; keep the passage's pastoral and historical context.
entries.morphologyStatus: Lexeme-level study only; no verse-specific inflection or parsing is asserted.

entries.contextualGloss: Obedience or attentive response; the word is used for responsive submission to a command or message.
entries.interpretiveCaution: Read the object and context of obedience; avoid turning the word into unqualified submission to human authority.
entries.morphologyStatus: Lexeme-level study only; no verse-specific inflection or parsing is asserted.

entries.contextualGloss: Adoption or placement as a son; Paul uses it for the status and inheritance believers receive in Christ.
entries.interpretiveCaution: The ancient legal and family imagery is important; do not imply that the metaphor limits God's welcome to male believers.
entries.morphologyStatus: Lexeme-level study only; no verse-specific inflection or parsing is asserted.

entries.contextualGloss: Face or presence; a common Hebrew noun used for a person's face and, in many contexts, presence or being before someone.
entries.interpretiveCaution: The word has a wide range and often appears in idioms; do not assign 'presence' mechanically to every occurrence.
entries.morphologyStatus: Lexeme-level study only; no verse-specific inflection or parsing is asserted.

entries.contextualGloss: Prayer or supplication; a noun used in biblical headings and prayers addressed to God.
entries.interpretiveCaution: Read the literary form and speaker; prayers include praise, confession, lament, petition and thanksgiving.
entries.morphologyStatus: Lexeme-level study only; no verse-specific inflection or parsing is asserted.
